goal: Stage 4 blockout and proxy rig from the approved clay views

outputs.name: reconstruction run record, attempt 1 (recon mv1 run.json: turned front view, body too wide, not used)
reconstruction run record, attempt 2 (recon mv2 run.json: forelegs fused, not used)

checks.title: Side proportions
checks.question: Side view at 57 cm to the top of the back: do the torso, chest to waist, neck, head, horns, tail and legs match the approved side clay?
checks.recommended: Approve the torso, neck, head and tail: measured on both silhouettes they agree within a few percent (length over rump height 1.78 vs 1.80, overall height 1.30 vs 1.30, chest depth 0.58 vs 0.58, waist 0.34 vs 0.32). One gap: the clay stands with its hind legs staggered (near foot back, far foot forward); the blockout stands square with both hind feet about 4 to 12 cm ahead of the clay average. I recommend keeping the square stance as the class rest pose; answer "move the hind feet back" and I rotate the hind legs back about 6 cm and re-bind.

checks.title: Front proportions
checks.question: Front view: narrow chest and forelegs, wider haunches and hind feet, horns spanning about 37 cm. Is the width right?
checks.recommended: Approve. The clay front is turned about 15 to 20 degrees with the tail swinging out, so the model was given its right half mirrored; that is why the outlines differ (box aspect 0.56 vs 0.94, overlap 0.26). Small faults left for stage 5 to resculpt: a thin whisker flap at the muzzle, and horns smooth and a little thicker than the slim ridged clay horns.

checks.title: Three-quarter proportions
checks.question: Three-quarter view from the standard 45 degree camera: does it read as the same animal as the approved three-quarter clay?
checks.recommended: Approve. The clay three-quarter is shallower (about 25 to 30 degrees off the side) than the standard camera, so the outlines differ (overlap 0.42); the masses agree with the side check.

checks.title: Pose sheet (shown, no decision needed)
checks.question: Rest, crouch, leap peak and landing, posed on the proxy rig. It bends without collapse; nothing to answer unless something looks broken.
checks.recommended: No action. Whole-body volume change: crouch -8.9 percent, leap -10.1, landing +1.1. Worst joint region -26 percent (hind shin in the crouch), under the 30 percent limit. Flagged: in the crouch and the leap the upper forelegs press into the chest (a visible crease, about 3,000 new touching triangle pairs); expected with no shoulder-blade joint, the stage 8 rig handles it.

checks.title: Hind-leg dominance
checks.question: Are the hind legs clearly the dominant mass: heavy thighs and long hind feet against slim short forelegs?
checks.recommended: Approve. Thigh 17 cm front to back against a 4.5 cm forearm (3.7 to 1); thighs stand 15 cm off the midline against a 7.7 cm waist half width; hind leg 63 cm of joint chain against 44 cm; hind foot 20 cm against a 10 cm fore paw. The clay side reads a little heavier because its two staggered hind legs add up in the outline; its thigh measures about 20 cm by eye.

report.method: reconstruction: Hunyuan3D-2 multi-view (hunyuan3d-dit-v2-mv, fp16, 50 steps, octree 380, guidance 5, seed 12345, CPU offload, torch capped at 4.72 GB with 1.08 GB held by other programs; peak 2.70 GB allocated, 3.17 GB reserved, so the card stayed near 5 GB of the 6.5 GB cap; 253 s). Three runs, all recorded: run 1 (front plus side) made a lopsided, too-wide body because the clay front view is turned 15 to 20 degrees; run 2 (front mirrored about the face midline, side, side mirrored as the right view) fused the forelegs; run 3 (front mirrored per row: face midline x 573 for the head, foreleg-gap midline x 597 for the body, blended over the neck; side; mirrored side) gave four separate legs, symmetric body, horns, ears and the full tail, so the parametric fallback was not needed. Masks: color distance from a quadratic background fitted to the image border (tolerance 22) plus a warmth test (the clay is warm gray, the ground and its cast shadow neutral) to drop the shadow; checked by eye on rendered overlays. Blender: largest piece kept (4 specks of 72 faces dropped), placed and scaled by 0.509 so the top of the back (the rump) is 0.570 m, 2 mm voxel remesh to one closed manifold, decimated to 200,000 triangles; 40 joints from the quadruped class via rig_modules with measured placements (tail 6 joints and paired horn joints per the tech spec); bone-heat weights, 4 influences, normalized, 0 unweighted vertices before any fix. tool: Hunyuan3D-2, Tencent Hunyuan 3D 2.0 Community License, noted per Nick's 2026-10-14 ruling that licensing is not a gate
